$comment: Powered 3-arm confirmation for the Q(U) settling lag, 40 paired seeds on simbench_lv_small pv_peak.

Arm {} = the default (symmetric tau=3 after the revert below); arm attack=3.0 is bit-identical to it and was the symmetric reference while {} still carried attack=0; arm settling=0 = the legacy instantaneous droop.

RESULT: the lag kills the limit cycle outright (ptp -0.024 pu, flips 29->0 on 39/40 seeds, duration -14.6 s, all p<1e-4) and improves the raw inversion signal priority_invariant_strict 0.375->0.575 (p=0.039). It costs ~1pp of electricity served on tiers 3-4 (p=0.010) and flips the gating priority_invariant on 6/40 seeds (p=0.031). That cost is REAL, not a shifting exclusion set (n_loads_throttled is 0 in both arms).

REFUTED: fast attack (attack tau=0) was meant to win the served energy back by clearing the opening over-voltage in one tick. It does not — el_served mean 0.959 vs the symmetric 0.974, duration +2.5 s, and one seed still limit-cycles. The bang-bang was delivering ~0.147 MVar of AVERAGE absorption vs the settled 0.031, so the headroom it bought needs a re-tuned Q(U) curve to recover, not a re-shaped lag. Default reverted to symmetric.
Judge on: tail-half avg_vm_pu ptp + flips (oscillation), electricity served by tier and claims__priority_invariant__passed (the regression), duration_s and events__qv_droop (cost).
name: ab_qv_droop_settling_wide
